summary: Flathead NF ridge lookout: 30-foot tower with living quarters planned in 1934, stationed 1936, camp and tower abandoned and gone; no current site description.

facts.design: Planned as a 30-foot tower with a house and living quarters on top (May 1934 newspaper report); firelookout.com lists a camp and a tower from the 1930s
facts.status_note: Abandoned and gone per firelookout.com; Gone per the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. The 30-foot height is the 1934 plan, not a measured height

staffing.status: a lookout was stationed on the tower (Missoulian item, July 1936)

events.note: Forest Service crew building a new lookout, planned as a 30-foot tower with a house and living quarters; completion not confirmed in the sources read (Kalispell Daily Inter Lake, May 1934)
A man was stationed on the Bar Z lookout the week of July 30, 1936 (Missoulian item)
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description refers to the Forest Service lookout tower on a bare north-south ridge, placing it in the Cabinet National Forest

Oct 1940 Sanders County Independent-Ledger item: a new lookout was under construction on Pine Mountain, about 1 1/4 miles from the earlier Barzee lookout site, which had only a tent and no regular cabin

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1940 survey description places the tower in the Cabinet National Forest; firelookout.com names the Flathead National Forest. The record keeps Flathead National Forest, the name on the later source, and the story reports both. The sources read do not say when the land changed hands.

notes_for_editor: height_m 9.1 in the record is the 30-foot height from the May 1934 plan (the record's source is the Ron Kemnow site); no as-built height was found, so the story says 'planned'. The 1934 and 1936 items are newspaper quotes on the Forest Lookouts page, not checked in the original papers. The 1940 survey text calls the forest the Cabinet National Forest. Two web searches and one page on the Flathead National Forest history (which names the Cabinet National Forest as a separate forest but does not give the change) gave no further detail. No register listing (NHLR or FFLOS) and no photo found. The FFLA list's 'Flathead' column is the county, not the forest, so the forest name rests on firelookout.com alone. The Oct 1940 Pine Mountain item (Sanders County Independent-Ledger, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page) says the earlier Barzee site had only a tent; it does not say whether the 1934 tower was finished, so the story keeps 'planned'. The Ron Kemnow source named for height_m is not in the sources list and was not checked.
